## Answer: 44

**Setup.** A hexagon on these six points is a cyclic ordering of them, and its signed area is $S/2$, where $S$ is the shoelace sum. Since $A=(0,0)$ contributes nothing to $S$, fixing $A$ as a vertex reduces $S$ to the sum of $x_k y_{k+1} - x_{k+1} y_k$ over the directed path through $B,C,D,P,Q$. Reversing the path negates $S$, so there are 60 distinct hexagons.

Using $T(X,Y)=x_Xy_Y-x_Yy_X$:

| Edge | $T$ | Edge | $T$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $B\to C$ | 100 | $D\to P$ | $-30$ |
| $B\to D$ | 100 | $D\to Q$ | $-60$ |
| $B\to P$ | 40 | $P\to Q$ | $-18$ |
| $B\to Q$ | 20 | $C\to P$ | 10 |
| $C\to D$ | 100 | $C\to Q$ | $-40$ |

I enumerated all 60 paths, then checked simplicity for each. Two diagonals ($A$–$C$ and $B$–$D$) cross each other, and many other pairs of edges cross, so most orderings are invalid.

**Maximum.** The largest $|S|$ among simple hexagons is 178, from the cycle $A,Q,P,B,C,D$ (or its reverse). Its vertices, in order, are $(0,0),(6,2),(3,4),(10,0),(10,10),(0,10)$. Shoelace gives $S=178$, so $a_{\max}=89$. This matches the square's area $100$ minus the dent of area $11$ cut by the path $A\to Q\to P\to B$.

**Minimum.** The smallest $|S|$ among simple hexagons is 90, from the cycle $A,B,C,Q,D,P$. Its vertices, in order, are $(0,0),(10,0),(10,10),(6,2),(0,10),(3,4)$. I checked that no two non-adjacent edges cross. Shoelace gives $0+100-40+60-30+0=90$, so $a_{\min}=45$.

**Difference.**
$$a_{\max}-a_{\min}=89-45=44$$

ANSWER: 44
